Answer: B
Reason: The CT image (Figure 2b) shows a heavily calcified, chronic-appearing obstruction of the right pulmonary artery (indicated by the arrow), which is characteristic of Takayasu arteritis rather than an acute thromboembolism. While pregnancy increases the risk of PE, the specific radiographic finding of arterial calcification points to a pre-existing chronic vasculitis as the cause of the patient's symptoms.
